items.title: Ray Sherman interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 13, 1998
items.q: I mean like I was on with Pete Fountain

ctx.x: Now do you still get — I don’t know if “residuals” is the correct word?

Yeah that was good, that I think that came in about 1968, well we started getting residuals for I guess the best thing was live T.V., which would be like the Hollywood Palace. If they show clips from that now we would get money. And I’ve noticed that a lot of — they’re doing Johnny Carson or what’s the gal the comedian that had a show — and they’re doing just I think it’s on The Family Channel. And it says you know, like re-runs of the Carson Show or something. And it’s just the comedy stuff. And I think they…

the theme, I think Tommy Newsom did that, so they spent money on that, but I mean like I was on with Pete Fountain, well he always had a singer, I mean he had music on his show, but evidently they just do the comedy skits on that, and that’s why, because they have to pay royalties, residuals. Now T.V. film, there’s still no residuals. Like all that stuff they play at Nick at Nite, which I did a lot of that, all those situation comedies from that period.
